Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-11-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2262002613", "name": "Yu Zhang"}, {"authorId": "7420251", "name": "Shuang-Rui Zhao"}, {"authorId": "2152571532", "name": "Yu-Long Shen"}, {"authorId": "2255872228", "name": "Xiao-Hong Jiang"}], "abstract": "Fast orbital motion in multi-orbit low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks causes highly dynamic satellite visibility and makes transmission satellite scheduling a fundamental challenge for downlink communication. This paper studies secure downlink communication with transmission satellite scheduling in a practical multi-orbit multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) LEO satellite network, where orbital-plane topology and a randomly located ground eavesdropper are jointly considered. We first characterize the temporal coupling between satellite visibility and scheduling decisions over consecutive time slots and design a transmission satellite scheduling scheme under the resulting coupling constraints. We subsequently establish a system-level effective secrecy rate (ESR) maximization model by incorporating the effective transmission factor to capture the impact of satellite scheduling, secure precoding, and power allocation, and formulate it as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. To tackle it, we develop a structure-aware Meta learning-empowered generalized Benders decomposition (GBD) approach, where the Meta learning mechanism is leveraged to accelerate the discrete scheduling sequence search in the GBD master problem, while the Lagrangian dual is utilized to derive the optimal continuous transmission configurations in the GBD primal problem. To further provide a low-complexity heuristic solution, we establish a switching admissibility criterion and propose the associated double-filter Tabu search, which prunes infeasible scheduling candidates with low computational overhead. Finally, extensive simulations on LEO constellations are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches in terms of ESR performance."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "f3951dfdc6359881a41f2819979a9c7e750e5204", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1007/s10586-026-06724-3", "CorpusId": 293251379}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f3951dfdc6359881a41f2819979a9c7e750e5204", "title": "An improved convolutional prototype network for open-set sound classification with limited data", "venue": "Cluster Computing", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: The following paper fields have been elided by the publisher: {'abstract'}. Lan"}], "abstract": "Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a critical tool for nondestructive detection and identification of subsurface targets. It enables efficient surveying and precise discrimination of buried objects through intelligent recognition techniques. However, in scenarios with limited data availability, current intelligent recognition models exhibit constrained generalization capabilities and demonstrate poor adaptability to new environments and tasks. Therefore, this article proposes a two-stage optimization adaptive and augmented model-agnostic metalearning (A2-MAML) approach for GPR target recognition with few-shot training. The proposed method introduces two key enhancements. An adaptive loss mechanism dynamically weights a supervised contrastive loss to improve generalization. A feature augmentation module is introduced to capture task-invariant representations. With only a limited number of training samples, the model achieves robust performance under noisy conditions and reduces the risk of overfitting. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of A2-MAML. Under few-shot settings, our method achieves $F1$ -scores of 88.5% for new environments (6-way-3-shot) and 89.7% for new tasks (4-way-3-shot). This represents relative improvements of 3.4% and 7.9% over the original MAML baseline. This gain underscores the superiority of our approach in data-scarce scenarios. A2-MAML delivers accurate recognition from very few samples, reducing costly field surveys and allowing rapid deployment across sites to offer clear practical benefits. The framework also demonstrates the potential for real-time deployment on IoT edge nodes due to its efficient inference capability."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "26cfa7144850481070b4b1bb36078e4221e25d51", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.21230", "CorpusId": 292982367}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/26cfa7144850481070b4b1bb36078e4221e25d51", "title": "Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21230, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-15", "authors": [{"authorId": "2511841689", "name": "Jie Li"}, {"authorId": "153253217", "name": "Youming Tao"}, {"authorId": "2256987771", "name": "Bo-Wei He"}, {"authorId": "2186828915", "name": "Meng Ding"}], "abstract": "Unlearning aims to remove selected knowledge from large language models to mitigate privacy and safety risks while preserving useful capabilities. For models that continue to be fine-tuned after release, this goal is insufficient: they must also resist relearning the deleted knowledge while preserving plasticity, the ability to learn new tasks. Existing defenses train against simulated relearning while trying to preserve useful capabilities, but low relearning alone cannot distinguish selective resistance from a general loss of plasticity. Evaluating preservation after an update requires deciding what the updated model should remain close to. A pre-update reference penalizes useful changes induced by the update simply because they depart from earlier outputs. We therefore formulate the reference-timing hypothesis that, at comparable target suppression, an update-matched reference better preserves plasticity than a pre-update one. To test and address this hypothesis, we propose Update-Matched Unlearning (UMU), which applies the same simulated relearning update to the defended model and to an undefended reference initialized from the same unlearned model, and uses new-task learning to guide model selection. Extensive experiments on TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen models show that UMU improves both relearning resistance and plasticity across all three base unlearning methods, lowering harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while raising new-task accuracy by 3.5 points. When the reference does not receive the update, relearning remains similarly low but new-task accuracy falls below the base method, supporting the reference-timing hypothesis and showing that robust unlearning should prevent recovery selectively without suppressing learning itself."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "61f725ee7bda41457ce1b10841dd3092645e3dde", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.22085", "CorpusId": 293003917}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/61f725ee7bda41457ce1b10841dd3092645e3dde", "title": "Coverage-Preserving Self-Healing in Partially Observable 3D UAV Swarm Networks via an Advection-Diffusion Graph Transformer", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22085, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-15", "authors": [{"authorId": "39974406", "name": "Dong-Bin Jiao"}, {"authorId": "2512270939", "name": "Zhi-Hao Li"}, {"authorId": "2223204507", "name": "Zong-Sheng Geng"}, {"authorId": "2966503", "name": "Dongdong Zhao"}, {"authorId": "2152939552", "name": "Sheng-Cai Liu"}, {"authorId": "2140364871", "name": "Shi Yan"}], "abstract": "This paper investigates the resilience and self-healing of unmanned aerial vehicle swarm communication networks under severe network partitioning in complex and adversarial environments. To address limited global observability after damage, we develop a damage-state inference mechanism that enables the ground control station (GCS) to infer global failures from sparse local reports without transmitting location-sensitive coordinates. To recover multi-cluster partitioned topologies, we then propose AdDiff-GT, a physics-inspired graph Transformer that incorporates advection-diffusion dynamics into a node-supernode hybrid graph. Local message propagation captures intra-cluster structural relationships, while global attention models inter-cluster interactions. A weighted composite loss jointly considers connectivity restoration, maneuvering cost, motion consistency, inter-cluster coordination, and spatial preservation during model training. We further develop a meta-learning strategy for transferable initialization across damage patterns and swarm scales, enabling efficient online GCS adaptation and distributed airborne inference. Simulations on 8,000 partitioned scenarios, including 5,000 large-scale cases, show that AdDiff-GT achieves effective topology recovery and spatial preservation over six representative baselines. Meta-learning reduces online planning overhead with a minor increase in recovery steps, balancing prior knowledge transfer and online adaptation."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "b8d439df8b171997f54811f4fd3638b8edcf077d", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.20294", "CorpusId": 292902597}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/b8d439df8b171997f54811f4fd3638b8edcf077d", "title": "MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20294, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-14", "authors": [{"authorId": "2243937605", "name": "Jun-Yi Zou"}, {"authorId": "2445701977", "name": "Avrova Donz"}], "abstract": "An agent can improve its behavior within an unresolved problem by changing how it acts and which experience it retains. We propose MMLA-RSI, a recursive self-improvement scheme with two implementations in Memory-Mediated Learning Architecture: Reasoning-Time Training (RTT) changes the policy state $\\Phi$, while Reasoning-Time Memory Adaptation (RTMA) changes authoritative memory $M$. Each route also makes its adaptation method an object of improvement. A current numerical updater trains the policy proposing its successor; a current memory manager chooses the records available to the process proposing its successor. An independently admitted successor takes over the same role in the next generation. We give bounded executable rule languages, shared task/proposal interfaces, and one algorithm for either route or their composition. The RTT instance changes scalar schedules in a clipped-momentum update. The RTMA instance chooses NULL or a complete-row write with possible eviction. A fixed interpreter, trusted committer, and independent evaluator bound what can change. State versions, read closures, and conditional properties describe causal execution, accepted transitions, and finite work. Existing numerical-component studies motivate the construction. In four-candidate program selection, retaining LARC feedback updates reduces expected error by 24.65 and 36.65 percentage points for two trained initializations. In chronological continuous-integration replay, feedback binding is positive while retention increases loss. Completed SQL studies improve substantially over an unadapted substrate but do not establish the required additional online benefit. These results characterize their declared components. The two recursive routes and their joint realization are specified here; their beneficial recursive chains and discovery efficiency remain to be evaluated."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "5713607e04fef401589fa1d46fc01d6a821f9554", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.20782", "CorpusId": 292982584}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/5713607e04fef401589fa1d46fc01d6a821f9554", "title": "Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20782, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-14", "authors": [{"authorId": "2290007522", "name": "Jian-Yu Zhang"}, {"authorId": "2253589498", "name": "L\u00e9on Bottou"}], "abstract": "The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. The analysis further predicts the need for a consistent inner learner, and the benefit of long contexts spanning related tasks. We test these claims on language models up to 8B, asking whether a model has a property (qualitative) rather than how much it wins (quantitative). Models that meet the requirements improve as data from related tasks accumulates; the rest degrade, and neither scale nor layer-type interleaving repairs this."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "e35b91e378355ce8f413d53b8caafa44552a8f01", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1021/acs.est.6c08192", "CorpusId": 293040297}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e35b91e378355ce8f413d53b8caafa44552a8f01", "title": "Why\nCan Cross-End Point Transfer Fail in Computational\nToxicology? Diagnosing Decision-Structure Incompatibility across 13\nEnd Points under Scaffold-Held-Out Evaluation", "venue": "Environmental Science &\nTechnology", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1021/acs.est.6c08192?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.6c08192, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content.
